title: Yellow Crystal Pendulum
subtitle: To the left, to the right, an arc and a fleeting gaze.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Excuse me.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Let me get through!
Train Station, Mor Pankh, 1966

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah! Will you move, please? For the sake of Marie Anne Lenormand!
The crowds on the platform are like schools of colorful sardines, pushing each other toward their destinations at an incredible speed.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh, finally! Ah-ah, ouch, this train ride gave me a real pain in the neck!
She finally gets to relax in one of the few empty seats in the station.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: How nice it'd be if I were to sleep on my bed in such cool and comfortable weather! Or I may as well just stay in Delhi with Mom to sell those topazes!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: *sighs*
Her fist tightens, though she doesn't consciously want to. The documents rattle in her hand.
She looks down at the documents.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: No! Matilda will not just give up here!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Who knows when they will approve my leave next time?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: These days, the celestial energy appears to be ideally strong, and the best observation area happens to be close to Delhi. What a heaven-sent opportunity for this genius of divination! Only the fools will take no action!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Wait and see. When I find the right place to meditate ...
She slightly shakes her fist. It seems she has made up her mind very seriously.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hum-humph, sooner or later, I will take my ride back to the top!
She rummages through the documents and moves close enough to read the poorly printed text.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Emm, let me see what this poster is about. Emm, Dīpa Festival?
She turns over the poster.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "People in Mor Pankh hold the Dīpa Festival during the meteor shower period every year to seek the blessings of Vindre."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh, so it's based on the meteor shower here! Vindre ... I think I have seen this name in the materials.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Now I'm in the east of Chandigarh. Can there be fewer signs here?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah-ha! This map has English on its back! Very nice. Would be more classy if they put French here instead.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: The place I found through divination is called Mor Pankh. It's a shrine! I need to go to its north cave?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Good. So, a shrine. Perhaps it has something to do with that comet myth I read about earlier. Isn't this also one of the places to see the upcoming meteor shower?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Great! This is where I am going, then. Where's my pen? Ah, here! Very good, let me put it down.
She hunches over and writes down something carefully.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Phew! Nicely done! Everything is a lot more convenient in the new town.
The ceiling looks new. This train station seems to have been built not too long ago.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Looks a lot better than the ceiling in Delhi's train station. I wonder how Mom and Dad are doing now. That Indian man can speak really fast when he's bargaining.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Emm.
As she slackens off, tiredness catches up with her.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Emm. Just one quick nap, very brief ...
Wow, cool! What a bold girl!
Hee hee ...
Guys, you see that? The girl brave enough to sleep in the train station.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Err, I see nothing, Boss! Not everyone has the great eyesight as yours. Oh, thank you. Nice monocular.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Oh, shiny jewels and wallet.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: But what is the thing she is holding so tightly, even when she's asleep? Isn't that the map they give away at the train station for free?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hmm, something valuable, I guess? Like the treasure map pictures in the books! If I can take a closer look ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Well, that's too hard for you. Ajar, you go from left, just as I taught you. Give me this gesture after you get it.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Heh-heh, no problem!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Do it well, boy! If you make it, that would be your first step to victory! Oh, remember, don't tell Ms. Sherjah I taught you these!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Go, go! Don't let other people get it before you do.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Umm ...?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What is it? Something swaying?
Sleepily, Matilda struggles to open her eyes and sees a little figure prowling away.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Emm, ahem! Is this yours, Miss?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Emm? Hey, that's the pendulum Mom gave me! Who are you?

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: It fell on the floor. I was just picking it up for you! There, don't lose it again.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh! Thank you ...
Matilda reaches for the pendulum.
Nuh-uh. It's yet too early to say thanks, girl.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: They find themselves in the shadow of a tall man.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: The man seems travel-worn, but he's carrying just a little luggage.
About three minutes ago? Or, five minutes ago? This fellow was wandering around you like a sneaky ferret-badger. Trust me. This is no friendly encounter.
He raises his left hand, more specifically, his prosthesis, to show the delicate wallet between those seemingly stiff fingers.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Umm? That's mine. You! You stole my wallet?!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Wha, what? I've put it in my pocket.
Someone needs to work on his techniques, right, boy?
The man catches Ajar's clothes—this time with his real hand—and easily picks him up.
Ajar is lifted in the air, but he isn't strangled with his collar, for the man has skillfully avoided the area of his neck.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Let go! Let go of me! D**n it! Go mind your own business!
Unfortunate for you, my business these days is to mind others' business. Seems like there are more things in that pocket of yours. Come on, you know where we are going.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Ah! Urrrh!
Ajar shows his teeth and bites the man hard on the right hand, which is dragging his collar.
Hiss—ah!
He lets go because of the pain. The little thief breaks free and quickly slips into the crowd.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: He's gotten away. My, my, my pendulum! He had my pendulum. Stop! You!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: *pants* D**n it! They are catching up!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Stop right there, you little thief!

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Humph!
The annoyed boy throws the pendulum into the distance with full strength.
Ah, you, boy! Wait!
The man runs into the colorful schools of sardines in hot pursuit.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: You! No! It's fragile. Don't!
In a beautiful arc, the transparent topaz falls toward the ground like a meteor.
Suddenly, a palm appears and catches it safely.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Phew. Just in time.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Is this yours?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah, yes.
The lady leans forward and speaks in a soft voice. Matilda stares into her eyes, completely abstracted.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Put it away, kid.
As she tilts her palm, the topaz falls swiftly into Matilda's hand.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah, thank you.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: It's okay.
The lady slightly nods and leaves like a gust of wind.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: She left so quickly.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah, the documents. Hope I didn't mess them up in the chase.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: One, two, emm? Two pages are missing. Where did they go?
A small, black-haird head is peeking from behind a pillar nearby.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Thankfully, I've planned my way out in advance. Well, at least Ajar won't be caught by anyone!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Good luck running away, poor Ajar.
She puts her palms together and wobbles her head to show her pity.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I will make a profit from her, including the part you failed to make. Humph, that easy mark with milky blonde hair, you'll see how Kanjira ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Whoa! What did I step on?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Is this the thing she was looking at? Yes, my eyes won't fail me.
Her face puckers up as she examines the paper in front of her.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: It really is a treasure map! Look here. She even drew a star, just like those pictures in books.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: You lucky girl, Kanjira. This is really something valuable!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Let me see. Oh, I have to read it together with the handwritten notes. What are these, hmm? She spelled these all wrong! Even added some lines above them.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Don't even bother trying. It's in French!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hey! Don't even think about taking my treasure, oh.
Matilda squints to scan the suspect, who is trying to avoid eye contact.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What were you muttering about with my map?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Emm, ahem.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I, uh, just pick it up and look for its owner. Hope I can help!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Help? Humph! Matilda needs no one's help! Not to mention from a girl who just showed up out of nowher- ... Hey! Don't ... don't touch me!
Kanjira ignores Matilda's contempt. She holds Matilda's arm intimately, with a big smile on her face.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Wow, you is so cool!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Is this your first time in the village? On your own? What's the plan? Sightseeing? Family visit? Or looking for some ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hey! Let go first. Why's that any of your business?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Umm, aha, I mean, perhaps not clear to you, but in fact, I am a guide who always give best service!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: A guide? Who always gives the best service?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: A tour guide, maybe? Anyways, I tell you, nobody know this village better than I!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Hey, don't stare at me like this. I'm wandering here for a reason: I only give services to outstanding and cool people. They have good taste!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: That why I find you at the station from all travelers! My most great, great customer ever!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Ah! The outstanding and impressive people, you say. Humph, at least you have sharp eyes.
Matilda tries hard to suppress her complacent smile.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: See, the place you is visiting is different from others!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: This shrine, only few tourists are willing to ... ahem, only the locals know! And now, people can only go into three caves out of four. But, if you choose I ...
The black-haired girl reaches out and pats the map on the star.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I can take you go north cave, even if it's not open!
Matilda frowns in response. There is suspicion in her eyes.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: How are you going to take me there?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: How, how I do that? Um, my local connections, of course!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I see. No wonder there were some discrepancies between the documents and the tourist brochure. Ah-ahem, well, of course, I knew this all along!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Heh heh.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hmm? What are you laughing at?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: No, no, no, my dear guest, it's just sneeze.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Well, you see, I just make a living here. I'm short and thin, can't compare with adults.
She tilts her head slightly—the angle is so perfect that it seems to be a result of countless practices—and sheds tears naturally.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: And you is so great. You will not let I, weak poor kid, get hungry for no money, will you?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Err. Even if you look at me with those puppy eyes ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: First sight I know, you is a lady with great taste, just like a sand cat, brave and smart.
Kanjira's downcast green eyes subtly steal a covert glance up at Matilda, secretly reading the signs on her face.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Sand, sand cat? It does sound like a smart animal.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Anyways, you is lucky to meet me, my lady!
Kanjira waves her hands as if she has made a big decision.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Well, well, for a great customer like you, I can only suffer some loss! Just 200 rupees, and I'll show you the shrine and the whole Mor Pankh village! With a special Dīpa Festival tour on the house!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Want me to recommend a hotel? I know good hotels, too.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Yes or no, my dear guest? My most great guest? Please ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Fine, fine. I will allow you to be my temporary assistant, for your life has been so sad already.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Yay! Let's go treasure hunting, hmm, sightseeing!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Excellent. Have you arranged a shuttle bus for the travel?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Heh heh, I have something gooder than bus for you!
Kanjira puts on a mysterious smile on her stained face.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: And I promise you, quick like flash!
